articles.title: Dialect-Robust Speech Language Models with Synthetic Pseudo-Dialect Augmentation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09321v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Speech Language Model (SLM) performance often degrades on dialects due to data scarcity. Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) augmentation struggles to cover diverse dialects as it requires a certain amount of real dialect speech. We propose synthesizing pseudo-dialect speech by converting LLM-generated dialect text via a standard-language TTS model, requiring zero real dialect speech. Additionally, we introduce intermediate standard-text prediction during training, acting as semantic normalization for downstream tasks. We evaluate dialect understanding via dialect-to-English speech translation across Japanese, German, and Chinese dialects. Compared to synthetic standard speech baselines, pseudo-dialect augmentation improves scores for Japanese (from 25.38 to 26.24) and German (from 31.57 to 32.47). Furthermore, the intermediate standard-text prediction effectively bridges the semantic gap, boosting performance to 28.26 for Japanese and from 11.67 to 16.37 for Chinese. These results suggest that our approach scales to various languages without requiring speech resources specific to each dialect.

articles.title: EASE: Entropy-Adaptive Distribution Shaping for Evading AI-generated Text Detectors
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09976v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: AI-generated text (AIGT) detection can be sensitive to the decoding choices of the source large language model (LLM). We observe that perturbing next-token logits or adjusting sampling temperature can reduce detection performance, providing a clear signal of detector vulnerability to decoding-time distribution changes. Building on this observation, we propose EASE (Entropy-Adaptive Distribution Shaping for Evasion), a training-free and detector-agnostic framework for evading AIGT detectors. EASE computes predictive entropy directly from the source LLM's next-token distribution and uses it to adapt both logit perturbation and sampling temperature, without detector feedback or model fine-tuning. Experiments across three source LLMs and multiple detectors demonstrate consistent reductions in detection performance, with negligible degradation in text quality and negligible inference overhead.

articles.title: RELATE: An Evaluation Framework for measuring Relational Orientation of Large Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09569v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for emotional support, raising concern that sustained use may draw users away from their real-world relationships. Yet existing evaluations primarily focus on the safety, empathy, or helpfulness of responses, leaving under-examined a relational question: where does the model orient the user for continued support? To address this question, we introduce relational orientation, a property operationalized through two non-exclusive dimensions: inward-facing (IF) language, which positions the AI as the user's ongoing source of support, and outward-scaffolding (OS) language, which encourages real-world human connection. Grounded in psychological and sociological literature, we formalize a taxonomy of relational orientation and present RELATE, a persona-conditioned framework for measuring inward-facing and outward-scaffolding language at the sentence level in multi-turn dialogues. RELATE pairs 76 help-seeking situations adapted from naturally occurring questions with three simulated user styles, providing 228 evaluation stimuli. In our experiments, we evaluate seven LLMs using dialogues with six assistant turns each, yielding 1,596 dialogues and 69,194 assistant sentences. We assess these sentences using a primary rubric-based LLM judge and apply a secondary judge to a subset. Under automated evaluation, we find that the proportion of sentences labeled as IF is higher at the sixth assistant turn than at the first, while the proportion labeled as OS is substantially lower for hesitant, indirect simulated users than for explicit, reassurance-seeking users. RELATE provides a reproducible framework and a sentence-level signal for auditing and steering the relational orientation of supportive LLMs.

articles.title: 主频5GHz麒麟不远了！余承东：会有更多华为手机采用基于韬定律的芯片
articles.text:
快科技10月9日消息，近日余承东在公开采访中明确表态，未来肯定会有更多华为旗下的手机产品，搭载这类采用逻辑折叠技术的自研芯片。
余承东透露，从已经发布的Mate XT 2三折叠手机开始，华为就正式引入了基于韬定律研发的逻辑折叠技术芯片，后续这类创新技术不会仅局限在少数旗舰机型上，会逐步下放到更多华为手机产品线当中。
他同时表达了自己的期待，希望国内整个半导体产业的配套产能能够进一步稳步提升，未来有足够的产能支撑，为中国乃至全球市场的消费者制造出更多体验领先的先进自研产品。
本次采访过程里余承东还首次公开了最新Mate 90系列手机搭载的麒麟9050 Pro芯片的详细参数，整台手机的综合性能相比上一代旗舰芯片直接提升了31%。
这款芯片里集成的巴龙调制解调器、图像信号处理器ISP、移动安全处理器MSP、灵犀架构CPU、Maleoon架构GPU，以及采用华为自研达芬奇架构做AI运算处理的NPU，所有核心模块全部都是华为自主设计研发。
余承东坦言，哪怕当前国内获取先进半导体制程工艺的外部环境仍有诸多限制，靠着全套的自主设计优化，这颗芯片依然实现了能效比的显著提升，整套系统的综合实际体验也远超出外界的预期。
除此之外，麒麟9050 Pro还搭载了华为独家研发的基于韬定律的逻辑折叠技术，通过垂直堆叠芯片的逻辑层，再利用层间的高密度互连线重构电路布局，直接缩短了芯片运算的关键路径，大幅降低了数据传输的时延。
按照韬定律公布的技术迭代路线，2026年推出的芯片性能核心频率将达到3.1GHz，目前上一代麒麟9030 Pro的P核主频为2.75GHz，下一代2026年发布的麒麟芯片峰值频率会提升12.7%，刚好落到3.1GHz的水平。
后续这条自研技术路线还会沿着既定节奏稳步迭代，后续的核心频率和晶体管密度都会保持稳步提升，到2031年预计就能实现每平方毫米400MTr以上的晶体管密度，同时旗舰芯片的主频可以突破5.0GHz。

articles.title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09209v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Substance Use Disorder (SUD) counseling requires patient responses that reflect underlying cognitive states such as beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness for change. Although large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent text, they often fail to produce cognitively coherent and clinically realistic patient behavior, especially under ethical and data-scarce clinical settings. Moreover, deploying frontier-scale LLMs in healthcare applications presents practical challenges including high computational cost, latency, privacy concerns, and limited deployability in resource-constrained environments, motivating the need for cognitively aligned small language models (SLMs). We propose a cognitively grounded framework for SUD patient dialogue generation that explicitly models and aligns latent cognitive components with patient histories and counselor questions. Our pipeline consists of two stages: cognitive component detection and cognitive component-aligned dialogue generation. To enable effective learning with smaller models, we combine knowledge distillation from high-capacity teacher models, preference optimization from human-annotations, and attention-guided reward shaping. Extensive evaluations using automatic scores like BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR and BLEU, and LLM-as-judge hit-metrics against both human and teacher-model references show that cognitively informed fine-tuning substantially improves cognitive realization and alignment over a generic instruction-tuned baselines and mental health domain specific SLMs, with particularly strong gains for open-ended cognitive components.

articles.title: SpaceX reportedly seeking $40 billion debt package for Nvidia AI hardware
articles.text:
SpaceX is reportedly looking to raise $40 billion to acquire Nvidia AI processors in a bid to expand its compute capabilities, reports the Financial Times. The financing could combine $10 billion in bank loans with $30 billion in investment-grade debt and may be completed in 2027, though discussions are still at an early stage and there is no guarantee that a transaction will materialize. If it does, then SpaceX's xAI will get $40 billion worth of Nvidia Rubin generation hardware, which includes AI accelerators.
Although Bloomberg reports that the proposed financing would be used specifically to purchase Nvidia AI accelerators, since xAI has traditionally bought servers or rack-scale AI solutions from Nvidia and its partners, it is likely that the company will continue to do so rather than opt to get accelerators and then build AI servers itself. Assuming that xAI indeed gets Vera Rubin NVL72 systems at around $8 million per unit, then for $40 billion it is going to get approximately 5,000 or so machines with roughly 360,000 Nvidia Rubin AI accelerators inside. At this point, it is unclear whether $40 billion is xAI's entire new compute capacity budget for 2027, or if the company plans to spend more.
The scale of xAI's Nvidia deployments is already substantial. Elon Musk said last month that xAI's Colossus 2 cluster currently houses 110,000 Nvidia GB200 accelerators and 440,000 GB300 devices.
SpaceX intends to obtain approximately $10 billion from banks and raise another $30 billion on the investment-grade debt market. Apollo Global Management is expected to take the leading role in arranging the financing, while bond manager Pimco is among a limited number of lenders discussing participation, the report claims. The transaction is currently expected to close sometime in 2027.
Apollo already has considerable exposure to this market and has already participated in financing the buildout of Elon Musk's AI infrastructure. In August, Nvidia teamed up with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish financing platforms designed to attract more than $500 billion in third-party funding for AI infrastructure. Bloomberg reports that Apollo had previously arranged a $7 billion financing deal with Musk's xAI that financed Nvidia hardware intended for the company's Colossus 2 data center near Memphis.
No parties mentioned in the story commented on the potential deal.

articles.title: Alice: A Large-Scale German Benchmark for Rubric-Based Multi-Dimensional Automatic Short Answer Scoring
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09661v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Automatic Short Answer Scoring (ASAS) is central to NLP for Education. However, openly available benchmarks remain scarce, and existing datasets largely address how well students answer a question directly rather than how well they master underlying concepts (knowledge elements) such as thermal energy or epistemic activities (skills) such as reasoning or claim.
To address this gap, we introduce Alice, a large-scale, rubric-based German ASAS dataset that is pedagogically aligned and comprises three subtasks: (i) learning performance (Alice-LP), (ii) knowledge elements (Alice-KE), and (iii) skills (Alice-SK).
We further formulate rubric-based ASAS as a rubric-retrieval task and benchmark the dataset with a range of language models, from encoder-only models to lightweight LLMs. We also benchmark the dataset with zero-shot prompting via LLMs and a standard classification baseline. The experiments show that LLMs, in particular, struggle to score knowledge elements and skills in the zero-shot setting. They also indicate that rubric text is often useful, especially for Alice-KE and Alice-SK, while on Alice-LP gains over sample-solution-focused inputs are more modest and vary by model and input format.

articles.title: Google Public Sector and SUNY launch AI-enabled platform to accelerate university research
articles.text:
Public research universities solve some of society’s most urgent challenges, but turning ideas into breakthroughs requires fast, secure access to cutting edge technology. In the agentic AI era institutions have an unprecedented opportunity to harness intelligent systems that can process massive datasets, run complex workflows, and dramatically accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.
Today at Gemini at Work, we’re announcing our collaboration with the State University of New York (SUNY) to launch the SUNY AI Platform, a secure AI and high-performance computing environment built on Google Cloud with Gemini Enterprise.
Initially available across nine of SUNY’s most research-intensive campuses, the platform is designed to help researchers move from hypothesis to discovery faster—and to help prepare New York’s students and workforce for an AI-driven economy.
Research with real-world impact
SUNY researchers are tackling challenges with direct impact for communities across New York and beyond. Their work includes improving weather prediction, detecting water quality issues, sequencing DNA for cancer treatments, and processing high-resolution brain scans to aid diagnosis.
To support that work, the SUNY AI Platform empowers researchers of all technical backgrounds to easily access and benefit from Google Cloud's advanced capabilities—bringing storage, high-powered computing, Gemini Enterprise, and more than 200 trusted AI models together into a seamless, centralized ecosystem. Rather than requiring individual teams and campuses to assemble these capabilities independently, researchers can work within a common foundation that helps simplify data analysis, enable collaboration across institutions, and apply consistent governance and responsible AI practices.
Equipping the SUNY community with AI-ready skills
Technology alone does not create impact; people do.
As part of this collaboration, SUNY is offering system-wide access to Google’s self-paced, industry-recognized AI credentials, available at no cost to students and faculty. Each course can be completed in 5-10 hours and requires no prior experience, helping learners build practical skills to write effective prompts, solve complex problems, and use AI tools responsibly. SUNY is also working to embed Google Career Certificates into academic programs so students can graduate with job-ready technical capabilities alongside their degrees.
Together, the SUNY AI Platform and these learning opportunities reflect a broader approach to AI adoption: pairing access to advanced technology with the skills and institutional capacity needed to put it to work responsibly.
To explore SUNY’s free AI learning tools and resources, visit suny.edu/google. Then watch our featured partnership video with Catherine Stollar Peters, SUNY’s Director of Research Data Strategy, to hear how academic leaders are using AI to transform education and the public sector.
You can also join us at the Google Public Sector Summit on October 20 to hear firsthand how leaders are using AI to transform organizations across the public sector.

articles.title: AMD seeks 'broader partnership' with Samsung as it looks to secure memory supply
articles.text:
A little less than seven months since signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) concerning memory supply and collaboration in various fields with Samsung, AMD's chief executive Lisa Su is visiting South Korea to secure additional supply of HBM memory for AI accelerators, reports Chosun.biz. Meanwhile, Samsung is seeking a broader partnership and 'hopes to turn its memory supply relationship with AMD into foundry' chip production orders, the report claims.
Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking
(Image credit: tsmc)
Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecks
Leading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and Samsung
ASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examined
Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined
"We are going to talk about our broader partnership," said Lisa Su when asked by reporters about what she planned to discuss with Samsung's executives. "We have many partners at Samsung."
Before visiting Samsung headquarters, Lisa Su and Jack Huynh, senior vice president and general manager of AMD's Computing and Graphics Group, attended the AMD Gamer Day event where Su and Huynh answered some questions from South Korean journalists and called local memory makers 'important strategic partners,' something that reflects the significance of data center-grade DDR5 and HBM memory for the company's AI and data center businesses.
"Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are key supply-chain partners for AMD," Su said, Chosun reports. "AI demand is extremely high, so we are planning our long-term supply chain with our partners. […] It is important to plan three to five years ahead with our partners."
The non-binding MOU that AMD and Samsung signed this March covered four areas and remained in effect for a period of three years:
Supply of next-generation memory products, including HBM4 and advanced DDR5;
Co-development and optimization of memory solutions for Al and high-performance computing systems;
Exploration of foundry manufacturing opportunities for the future AMD platforms;
Co-optimization of advanced packaging and related semiconductor technologies.
While Samsung has become a principal supplier of HBM4 for AMD's Instinct MI400-series accelerators, expansion of collaboration beyond memory supply is considerably more complicated, as it involves considerable efforts to design chips for Samsung Foundry's process technologies as well as risks associated with a product ramp at a new contract chipmaker. Truth to be told, AMD already uses Samsung Foundry and UMC to make its "ICs in the form of programmable logic devices" however, moving production of more advanced products to Samsung is risky. Meanwhile, Samsung badly needs big customers like AMD, and the latter's dependence on HBM supply certainly gives the former leverage.
"If we transition the production of some of our products to new manufacturers, we may experience delayed product introductions, lower yields or poorer performance of our products," AMD wrote in its most recent Annual Report.
AMD has already started shipments of its Instinct MI455 accelerators with 432GB of HBM4 memory onboard as well as rack-scale Helios AI systems to interested parties.
"We have started shipping our next-generation MI455 and Helios systems," Su told journalists, according to Chosun. "These are all systems that use HBM4."
So, it looks like the company is negotiating for more memory supply. The question is, will it take a risk and adopt Samsung Foundry for something more serious than niche programmable chips in a bid to get more high-bandwidth memory and sell more expensive AI accelerators? Only time will tell.

articles.title: The Persona Hierarchy Model: Understanding Contextual Generalization in Fine-Tuning LLMs
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.09384v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Language models are routinely fine-tuned under a fixed context, such as a generic system prompt, persona or domain-specific instruction, yet the learned behavior sometimes stays confined to that context and sometimes broadly generalizes to unseen contexts. We propose the Persona Hierarchy Model to explain this: a shared default persona influences behavior across contexts. Under this model, fine-tuning that modifies the shared persona promotes broader transfer, whereas changes to local personas remain more context-specific. Across 120 fine-tuned models spanning four behaviors and 15 training contexts, generalization narrowness positively correlates with the similarity between the training context's persona and the default persona (Pearson's r = 0.72 for Qwen3-4B). Prior fine-tuning under the default context can broaden generalization in subsequent training under other contexts. Aligning contextual responses with default-persona responses produces stronger effects. Finally, we propose persona-preserving regularization (PPR) to confine undesired contextual generalization. In RL, PPR cuts reward hacking from 42-55% to at most 0.2% under every evaluated prompt while retaining accuracy gains. These results support the Persona Hierarchy Model as an explanation for contextual generalization and can motivate future controls on unintended generalization for better alignment of LLMs.

articles.title: Claude最强迷你模型登场，价格暴降90%，直逼DeepSeek？
articles.text:
智东西
编译 | 程茜
编辑 | 云鹏
智东西10月8日消息，今日凌晨，Anthropic发布其迄今最便宜、最快且功能最强大的迷你模型Claude Haiku 5.5，平均运行成本比Claude Haiku 4.5低约75%。
Anthropic的官方博客称，Claude Haiku 5.5适用于高吞吐量且对成本敏感的任务，可以处理快速且重复性的工作负载，例如摘要生成、数据整理、数据库查询、分类任务、实时客户支持以及浏览器相关操作等。Haiku 5.5也可以和Sonnet 5.5搭配，作为编程工作的子智能体使用。
在Artificial Analysis上， Haiku 5.5在AI分析指数上得分为43，在最高性能模式下，得分略高于GLM-5.3 Flash（42分）、Gemini 3.8 Flash（41分）和GPT-6 Luna（38分）。
Claude Haiku 5.5不超过10万token时的输出价格比DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash空闲时段还要便宜。
Claude Haiku 5.5的定价比Claude Haiku 4.5低90%，适用于请求量不超过10万个token的情况；而超过10万个token的请求可享受50%的折扣。在Claude Haiku 4.5版本中，有90%的请求属于上述范围。
此外，Anthropic还对全系模型性价比进行了优化，其将Claude Sonnet 5.5的缓存读取操作价格下调至一半，即每百万个token只需支付0.1美元（约合人民币0.67元），在大多数智能体任务场景下，其运行成本降低约20%；Claude Max和Team订阅用户还将拥有新的月度API积分奖励。
Claude Haiku 5.5现已可在所有平台上使用，包括Amazon Web Services、Google Cloud和Microsoft Azure。在Claude平台上，开发者可以立即开始使用claude-haiku-5-5。
一、动画效果实测惊艳，但部分场景比GPT-6 Luna贵12倍
不少开发者实测对比了Claude Haiku 5.5和GPT-6 Luna的表现。
一位开发者生成了斑马在奔跑的动画，其中从斑马的花纹、形态到背景，Haiku 5.5生成的画面都更为和谐自然。
另一位网友实测了Haiku 5.5和Sonnet 5.5作为子智能体协同使用，在下方的案例中，两个模型协同只花了不到1分钟就完成任务。
有开发者对比发现，Claude Haiku 5.5在相同场景下的成本是GPT-6 Luna的12倍。
下图中两个项目的API价格相同，在Claude Haiku 5.5平台上构建同一个动画化的体素式3D宝塔岛屿需要24.96美元（约合人民币167.27元），在GPT-6 Luna平台上为1.91美元（约合人民币12.8元）。
另一位开发者使用Haiku 5.5与GPT-6 Luna生成了夜班列车动画。GPT-6 Luna在54.6秒内以低于0.01美元（约合人民币0.07元）的价格，生成了上面的内容，列车在夜间的森林里运行，摄像机还会切换远景、近景。
Haiku 5.5则使用了5分钟12秒，成本为0.03美元（约合人民币0.21元），但开发者放出的案例中Haiku 5.5只生成了一张火车的静态图。
综合来看，Haiku 5.5在绝大多数上下文不超过10万token的自动化任务、浏览器与计算机操作、轻量智能体场景下可以实现更优的综合收益。但面对更为复杂，需要重度编程、极高复杂度的多步规划任务时，其能力仍存在短板，这类场景依旧需要选用更高阶模型来保障输出质量。
二、相比上代模型得分几乎翻倍，整体可对标GPT-6 Luna
Anthropic放出的基准测试表中，对比了Haiku 5.5与Haiku 4.5、GPT-6 Luna、Sonnet 5.5在知识工作、计算机操作、多学科推理、智能体编程、视觉推理等方面的表现。
8项基准测试中，Haiku 5.5的表现均超过了Haiku 4.5、GPT-6 Luna。其中相对于上一代的Haiku 4.5，Haiku 5.5的知识工作得分几乎翻倍，Terminal‑Bench智能体编程得分从0%上涨到39.2%，这说明Haiku 5.5已经具备较强的智能体能力。
整体来看，Haiku 5.5综合性能相比GPT-6 Luna更强，尤其在OSWorld电脑操作测试中具有明显优势。Haiku 5.5距离高端模型Sonnet 5.5仍有差距。
Haiku 5.5是Anthropic首款支持可调算力档位（adjustable effort setting）的Haiku系列模型。用户可以自主选择优先优化成本，或是优先优化模型智能度。
▲Haiku 5.5在不同算力档位下，三项基准测试的表现。
定价方面，Anthropic称，当提示词长度不超过10万token时，Haiku 5.5的性价比尤为突出。
下图展示了Haiku 5.5与Anthropic更先进模型之间的关键差异。
对于需要复杂智能体编程任务的场景，如那些通过Terminal-Bench 4.0进行评估的任务，Sonnet 5.5和Opus 5.5仍然是更好的选择。Haiku 5.5则更适合那些范围较为狭窄的任务，这些任务在Claude的先前版本中可能会因为成本过高而难以实现，比如压缩、摘要处理或子智能体工作等任务。
此外，本周Anthropic将向所有Max和团队订阅者提供新的月度API信用额度，供他们在Claude平台上使用。使用Max 5x的用户每月可获得100美元（约合人民币670元）的信用额度，使用Max 20x的用户则每月可获得200美元（约合人民币1340元），团队订阅者最多可获得500美元（约合人民币3350元）的信用额度。
面向开发者，他们同时更新了Claude Python与TypeScript SDK，新增计算机操作与浏览器操作的测试版能力支持。
三、对齐错误案例减少，Haiku 5.5网络安全保护更严格
Claude Haiku 5.5在几乎所有对齐评估指标上都取得了显著改进。相比上一代模型，研究人员发现的对齐错误案例大幅减少，同时，模型在应对错误行为时的协作意愿也更强。
根据其功能特性，Haiku 5.5的网络安全保护措施比Haiku 4.5更为严格。在网络安全方面，这些措施允许执行更广泛的防御任务，但无法阻止攻击者进行的渗透测试及其他攻击手段。
Haiku 5.5的生物安全机制与Sonnet 5、Sonnet 5.5以及Opus 5相同。这些机制允许研究相关生物学问题，但会限制那些可能带来危害的请求的访问权限。
结语：轻量模型也要有智能体能力，小模型不再只追求“便宜够用”
时隔一年，Anthropic更新了自家迷你模型，并升级了智能体能力，这或许将改写过去小模型主打“便宜够用”的定位，如今Haiku 5.5补齐了计算机操作、终端编码、图表推理短板，搭配可调推理档位，可以用更低成本承接10万token以内的智能体业务。
这意味着AI智能体开发的成本门槛被进一步压低，开发者不必动辄调用高价主力模型来做网页浏览、桌面自动化这类高频任务。不过值得注意的是，Haiku 5.5依然存在能力边界，在复杂场景高端模型的价值依旧不可替代。
未来，轻量模型或许也会成为智能体产品规模化落地的主力选型，这也会倒逼各家厂商在低成本智能体赛道加速竞争。
来源：Anthropic、X

HarmonyOS 7升级持续推进！Mate 60、Pura 70等多款老机型开放尝鲜
articles.text:
快科技10月8日消息，据华为官网HarmonyOS 7支持机型页面显示，目前已有多款老机型进入系统升级尝鲜名单，包括Mate 60系列、Mate X5系列、Pura 70系列等热门产品。
具体来看，此次涉及的手机包括华为Mate 60系列、Mate X5系列、初代Mate XT非凡大师、Pura 70系列、Pocket 2系列，以及nova 14系列和nova 16 SE等机型。
除了手机，华为MatePad Pro 13.2英寸2025款、MatePad Pro 12.2英寸2025款，以及部分MatePad Air、MatePad 11.5 S平板也在支持名单中。
作为华为新一代操作系统，HarmonyOS 7在界面设计、AI能力和系统性能等方面都带来了新的变化。
其中，系统加入了全新的沉浸光感设计，拖动图标时，光影会跟随手指移动，滑动清除通知时也会出现粒子消散效果。同时，3D空间壁纸、空间时钟等功能进一步丰富了锁屏界面的视觉效果
AI方面，小艺升级为系统智能体，能够调用更多系统能力处理复杂任务，并通过小艺导航条提供主动服务，让日常操作更加方便。
此外，HarmonyOS 7还进一步优化了方舟引擎，提升应用启动、后台保活及多任务切换体验。星盾安全也加入了更多AI防诈能力，可针对诈骗通话、风险网页等场景提供安全提醒。

articles.text: 受科技企业争相建设高速AI数据中心带动，Lumentum Holdings Inc. 的光电器件产能几乎已经全部售罄，订单覆盖至2029年。今年早些时候，英伟达向Lumentum及其竞争对手Coherent各投资20亿美元。该公司主营先进磷化铟器件，支撑高速云计算与数据传输业务。总部位于加州圣何塞的 Lumentum 首席执行官迈克尔・赫尔斯顿周五在东京接受采访时表示，部分产品明年仍有约70%的需求无法满足，另有部分产品到2028年还有30%的需求缺口。（新浪财经）

articles.title: 从「小而专」切入，3C 卖家如何在东南亚做深配件生意
articles.text:
一条音频线、一枚转接头，看似是消费电子市场中不起眼的小配件，却对应着消费者真实而具体的使用需求。
对于3C配件市场而言，产品标准化程度较高。头部品牌通常会集中资源布局需求体量较大的核心产品，而一些应用场景更加细分的产品，品牌化供给相对有限。消费者如果希望兼顾品质与价格，选择往往并不多。
2018年成立的深圳市SUNKANDI科技有限公司，最初主要从事消费电子品牌代理和渠道业务。2024年下半年，公司开始开发自有品牌SUNKANDI，并陆续在线上平台销售，产品覆盖音频线、音频转接产品、数据线、各类转接头以及办公周边等消费电子配件。
在SUNKANDI总经理Jack Wang看来，与其在成熟赛道中单纯追逐销量，不如从仍然存在的细分需求中寻找机会。“我们希望从这些更加细分的需求切入，让消费者在一些相对冷门的消费电子配件上，也能够拥有兼顾品质和性价比的品牌化选择。”
01
不只追逐爆款，从细分需求寻找产品机会
从代理商转向自有品牌后，SUNKANDI并没有一开始就将目光集中在市场规模最大的产品上，而是尝试从自身熟悉的音频配件领域切入。
“我们最开始还是立足于原有供应链优势，把音频线和音频配件做得比较系统。”Jack介绍，目前SUNKANDI仅不同类型的音频转接线，就已经布局了约60至70款产品。
在Jack看来，一些成熟的消费电子配件已经进入充分竞争阶段，市场上的产品较为丰富，但对于一些更加细分的需求，头部品牌未必愿意持续投入研发，小型卖家又可能缺少投入模具和产品开发的能力。
这恰恰成为SUNKANDI寻找机会的地方。
即使是一条客单价并不高的音频线，SUNKANDI也愿意投入几千元甚至上万元重新开发模具，通过产品外观、工艺以及使用体验上的差异，做出与市场通货有所区别的产品。
这种思路也让SUNKANDI逐渐调整了自己的产品策略。品牌早期也曾尝试从普通3.5毫米音频线等市场规模较大的产品切入，但随着实际经营推进，团队发现这类产品竞争较为激烈，于是开始将更多精力放在RCA音频线、6.35毫米乐器线等更加细分的产品上。
“我们现在越来越认为，3C配件已经进入更加‘重产品’的阶段。”Jack说。
在他看来，一些细分产品虽然整体市场体量没有那么大，但消费者需求比较明确，竞争也相对缓和。SUNKANDI希望先从这些细分产品建立一定的销量、品牌和店铺基础，再逐步进入竞争更加激烈的主流产品市场。
与此同时，丰富的产品矩阵也让SUNKANDI能够根据不同市场的需求进行调整。例如，新加坡、马来西亚消费者拥有较多传统音频设备，因此对于RCA、6.35毫米接口、乐器线等产品的需求更加丰富；泰国、越南消费者则更多关注Type-C、3.5毫米接口等与移动设备相关的音频产品。
因此，SUNKANDI并没有用一套固定的产品组合覆盖所有市场，而是先通过较为丰富的产品矩阵覆盖不同需求，再根据当地实际销量筛选重点产品。
（图源：卖家供图）
02
从“卖出去”到“更快送到”，
本地履约成为增长拐点
产品差异化之外，SUNKANDI也逐渐将竞争力延伸到履约环节。
东南亚是SUNKANDI较早开展跨境业务的市场，公司最初的跨境业务就是从东南亚发展起来，后来才逐步拓展到其他平台和市场。对于SUNKANDI而言，东南亚既有此前积累的业务基础，消费者部分消费习惯也与国内市场较为接近，因此成为自有品牌重点布局的市场之一。
在平台选择上，SUNKANDI也将Shopee作为核心经营平台。随着品牌逐步进入市场，团队开始进一步关注消费者从下单到收货的完整体验，并将本地化履约作为重点投入方向。
品牌运营最初大约半年的时间里，整体销售相对平稳。随后，SUNKANDI开始尝试海外仓。“商品进入海外仓之后，订单增长开始变得比较明显，这是我们的第一个重要拐点。”Jack回忆。
其中，一款爆款产品的表现让团队更加直观地看到了本地化履约带来的变化。进入本地仓之前，这款产品一个月销量大约在1000件左右；转向本地化履约后，月销量增长到了2000多件，整体销量实现了明显提升。
“这也进一步验证了我们对于本地化履约的判断。”Jack表示。对于体积小、单价不高的3C配件而言，SUNKANDI认为，更快的配送速度不仅能够改善消费者购物体验，也有助于提升商品转化。
为了进一步提高履约效率，SUNKANDI甚至愿意为部分销量并不高的细分SKU提前进行本地备货。Jack介绍，即使一些冷门SKU一个月可能只有几十件销量，只要已经验证存在稳定需求，团队也会考虑进行本地备货。
早期进行大规模本地备货时，SUNKANDI单月投入本地库存的货值就达到20多万元，接近30万元。随着不同站点和SKU不断增加，如何更精细地管理库存，也成为团队必须解决的问题。
为此，SUNKANDI根据不同站点、不同SKU、历史销量、大促节点以及仓储运输时效等因素，逐步建立了一套内部库存管理表格。如今，只需要输入一个产品的历史销量、站点情况和运输周期等数据，团队就能够计算相对合理的备货量。
“这套方法看起来并不复杂，但实际上是团队经过几个月不断调整、验证和修正以后形成的。”Jack说。
除了本地化履约，SUNKANDI与Shopee客户经理建立更深入的沟通，也成为店铺经营中的另一个变化。早期团队主要依靠自身摸索平台运营，随着沟通深入，客户经理在营销活动、经营数据以及本地化履约等方面提供了更加明确的建议，对后续店铺增长带来帮助。
目前，SUNKANDI也在客户经理的建议下继续提高本地化履约比例，并进一步增加Shopee官方仓的使用。
这种围绕产品、履约和运营能力的持续投入，也在大促节点中得到进一步验证。今年9.9大促当天，SUNKANDI整体销售成绩在原有基础上又实现翻倍。对团队而言，这一表现也进一步增强了其继续投入产品开发、本地履约和精细化运营的信心。
（图源：卖家供图）
03
从产品研发到消费者沟通，把细分优势做成品牌能力
对于3C配件而言，消费者购买时往往需要判断接口、功率、适配设备等信息。产品本身虽然小，但信息是否准确完整，可能直接影响消费者能否选择适合自己的商品。
因此，SUNKANDI从产品设计研发阶段就开始建立较为完整的产品资料。每一个产品都会对应一份产品规格书，功能、参数、适配设备以及包装等信息都会进行标准化整理。
新品正式上线后，运营、客服和售后团队都可以基于这套资料与消费者沟通。与此同时，团队每个月还会整理客服和售后反馈，将消费者实际遇到的兼容性、使用方式等问题记录下来，再持续补充到产品资料以及后续产品开发中。
商品视觉方面，SUNKANDI也按照成熟消费电子品牌的标准制作产品图片和建模渲染，希望尽可能完整、准确地呈现商品信息。特别是在功率、接口和参数等方面，团队要求商品页面展示的数据必须与真实产品能力保持一致，不通过夸大参数获取短期转化。
“我们希望消费者无论是在商品页面还是咨询客服时，都能够获得准确、统一的信息。”Jack表示。
品牌初期，SUNKANDI也持续进行营销投入。品牌刚开始运营的3-5个月，每个月的营销和运营投入可以达到GMV的20%-30%左右，通过前期投入逐步建立品牌和店铺基础。
目前，SUNKANDI已经积极参与AMS联盟营销，并能够为店铺带来一定比例的订单。随着店铺基本盘进一步稳定，团队也计划增加Shopee Video短视频、Shopee Live直播等内容形式，让营销方式从基础的上新和广告投放进一步向内容营销延伸。
（图源：卖家供图）
04
深耕现有市场，再寻找新的产品与增长空间
对于未来的东南亚消费电子市场，SUNKANDI也在寻找新的产品机会。
Jack认为，AI和智能化可能成为消费电子领域未来的重要发展方向。随着AI逐渐影响更多行业，传统消费电子产品也可能产生新的智能化应用场景，一些过去功能相对单一的配件，未来或许会出现新的使用方式。
移动办公也是团队关注的另一个方向。随着移动办公在新加坡、马来西亚等东南亚市场逐渐出现更多相关需求，便携式、移动化的办公周边以及消费电子配件也可能获得新的发展空间。
市场拓展方面，SUNKANDI目前已经布局新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、菲律宾、越南等站点，并正在积极拓展巴西市场，同时持续关注Shopee新开放站点带来的机会。
不过，相比单纯扩大市场范围，团队现阶段仍然希望先把现有产品和重点站点做深。
面对下半年大促，SUNKANDI已经提前进行库存、产品和团队方面的准备。9.9所需库存从7月开始准备，11.11、12.12的库存也将提前推进；产品方面，团队正在开发两大重点产品方向以及十多个更加细分的产品；团队方面，则继续补充运营和助理人员，并引入ERP等经营管理工具，将过去经营过程中积累的方法进一步标准化。
从消费电子品牌代理商，到打造自有品牌；从主流产品之外的细分需求，到持续投入模具和产品研发；再从跨境销售到本地化履约，SUNKANDI正在逐步形成一套自己的品牌经营方法。
对于Jack和团队而言，3C配件的机会并不只存在于销量最大的产品中。那些看似细小、但真实存在的消费需求，同样可以成为品牌持续深耕的空间。而在Shopee等平台上，产品、履约与运营能力的不断积累，也正在帮助SUNKANDI从一个消费电子配件卖家，逐步走向更完整的品牌化经营。
